entries.5eab0da4cf944f44: To keep a plant operating, instruments that measure temperature, flow rate and pressure, a control system that issues instructions to valves and pumps based on those values, and a system that continues to record whether there are any abnormalities are needed at the same time. Yokogawa Electric Corporation delivers these 3 not as separate products but as 1 package. The report describes the contents of the Control Business as “comprehensive solutions, from field sensors to production control systems, programmable controllers, industrial recorders, various software for improving productivity, and services that minimize plant life cycle costs.” At the center is CENTUM, the integrated production control system announced in June 1975. The Measuring Instruments Business differs in character from this: it is a business that sells equipment used 1 unit at a time at research and development sites.
entries.5ec6418dbb4e8788: Operating profit in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥82,555 million, down 1.2% from the previous year. Operating profit by segment was ¥75,155 million for the Control Business and ¥7,792 million for the Measuring Instruments Business, while New Businesses and Other had an operating loss of ¥391 million. The rankings by net sales and by profit coincide, and the Control Business accounts for most of both sales and profit. The company explains the reason operating profit decreased as "while gross profit increased with the increase in net sales, factors such as a deterioration in the gross profit margin, including one-time factors mainly in the Control Business, acted as downward pressure," and adds that excluding the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations, it increased by about ¥800 million from the previous fiscal year. The Measuring Instruments Business grew at a different pace, with net sales up 13.6% and operating profit up 25.2% from the previous fiscal year, faster than the Control Business. New Businesses and Other has not yet generated profit, and its loss increased from ¥282 million in the previous year to ¥391 million.

entries.946b6718666762f4: It is a company that sells systems that measure “what is happening now” inside factories and plants and keep equipment operating based on those values. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that since its founding in 1915 it has “provided cutting-edge products and solutions to industry, centered on measurement, control and information technologies.” What it sells is not only equipment. Flowmeters and pressure transmitters placed on site, production control systems that operate them together, and everything from installation and engineering to maintenance over decades form 1 [[term:segment|segment]] (the Control Business), and of net sales of ¥604,829 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026, the Control Business accounts for about 94%, the Measuring Instruments Business for about 6%, and New Businesses and Others for about 1%. Its sales destinations are not any 1 specific company but specific industries. The report states about the Control Business that it “has a high share in Japan through diverse industry development, including oil, gas, chemicals, electric power, steel, pulp and paper, pharmaceuticals and food,” and continues that it “has a high share in resource countries and emerging countries such as the Middle East, China and ASEAN countries, centered on upstream and downstream.” Its overseas net sales ratio in fiscal 2025 was about 73%, and it is a company for which overseas is far larger than Japan. Because a plant, once built, operates for decades, the report explains that it is “increasing the weight of solutions that lead to improving the productivity of customers' existing plant equipment and to making maintenance more efficient, by utilizing its abundant delivery record.” Its track record itself — having handled more than 30,000 projects around the world — is an asset that calls in the next work.

entries.a91f9c24e7e8991b: This is the business that takes on, as a whole, the mechanisms for measuring and keeping large plants, such as oil and chemical plants, running. The [[term:annual-securities-report|Annual Securities Report]] states: "We provide comprehensive solutions ranging from field sensors such as flowmeters, differential pressure and pressure transmitters and process analyzers, to production control systems, programmable controllers, industrial recorders and other equipment, various software for improving productivity, and services that minimize the life cycle cost of plants." Its feature is that the instruments placed in the field, the control systems that run them together, and the services that keep them running form 1 business, with the integrated instrumentation and control system CENTUM, announced in June 1975, at its center. The products are made by Yokogawa Manufacturing Corporation, Yokogawa Electric Asia Pte.Ltd., Yokogawa Electric (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. and others, and they are sold, installed and maintained by Yokogawa Solution Service Corporation in Japan and by local subsidiaries in Southeast Asia, Europe, North America, the Middle East and Africa, and China overseas. Net sales to external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥565,523 million, accounting for 93% or more of the company's total net sales of ¥604,829 million. Segment profit was ¥75,155 million, and the number of employees was 17,504 (temporary employees of 2,299 are shown separately). Orders received were ¥570,881 million and the order backlog was ¥453,396 million; the order backlog approaches 1 year of sales because the work is delivered over a long time for each project. The company explains that orders and net sales both increased, mainly owing to winning large projects in Japan against the backdrop of solid energy demand, while operating profit decreased by ¥2,426 million from the previous year owing to a worsening gross profit margin including one-time factors.
entries.aef84e0e5d31de67: A business that manufactures and sells measuring instruments that accurately measure the form of electrical and optical signals. The annual securities report lists its main products as waveform measuring instruments, optical communication-related measuring instruments, signal generators, and power, temperature and pressure measuring instruments; unlike the Control Business for plants, these are devices used one unit at a time at research, development and production sites. They are manufactured by Yokogawa Manufacturing Corporation and others, and sold in Japan by Yokogawa Test & Measurement Corporation and overseas by local subsidiaries in Southeast Asia, Europe, North America and China. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥34,006 million, segment profit was ¥7,792 million, and the number of employees was 729 (134 temporary employees are shown separately). Its share of company-wide revenue is about 6%, but it is growing faster than the Control Business: revenue rose 13.6% year on year and operating profit rose 25.2% year on year. Orders rose 38.5% year on year to ¥41,974 million, and order backlog swelled to ¥12,783 million, 290.9% of the prior-year level and nearly three times as large, which the company says was mainly driven by increased demand related to AI data centers.
